_note: Retrieval evaluation set for the synthetic corpus. 'expected' lists the approved study codes a good answer should draw on; 'negative' questions have no relevant study and should retrieve nothing. 'near_negative' questions name a product the corpus covers but ask about something no study measures (a second store, a card's design): similarity alone cannot reject them, so they are reported separately. In briefs the topicality check drops them (hashing) or caps confidence (semantic embedders). Paraphrase and Taglish questions avoid the findings' own wording on purpose: that is the failure S&I described in their keyword search. 'split' puts each question in 'tune' (used to choose floors and rerank weights) or 'holdout' (reported, not tuned on), alternating within each set. Each half has about 20 questions: treat a held-out difference of one question as noise.
